newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi excludes confidence vote on budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi excludes confidence vote on budget.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Thursday that the government would not call a confidence vote to speed the passage of the 1997 budget bill through the lower house of parliament.
He also signalled he did not expect the bill to clear the house before the weekend.

Asked if the government would call a confidence vote to hasten the budget's passage through the Chamber of Deputies, Prodi told reporters: "No, because we are patient. Everything will be finished on Sunday."
The government coalition does not have an absolute majority in the lower huse and relies on support from the hardline Communist Refoundation party in the lower house.

The budget's passage through the Chamber was facilitated earlier this week after the centre-right opposition boycotted the debate there in protest against the package, which aims to cut 62.5 trillion lire off next year's budget.
The bill subsequently goes to the Senate for ratification, with full parliamentary approval due by the end of the year.
